Order 
IA No. 772/2019, an application filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay, is taken up for consideration.
2. Upon due consideration and for the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed.
The delay in filing the present appeal is hereby condoned.

3. This appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 04.08.2018 passed by the VIII Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as the "Claims Tribunal"), Gwalior (M.P.), in Claim Case No. 127/2014.

entities.text: VIII Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appeal is filed on the ground of inadequacy of compensation, seeking enhancement thereof.
4. The date of the accident, negligence, and the issue of liability are not in dispute.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, a compensation of Rs. 78,130/- has been awarded in respect of the death of the deceased- Baijnath Singh Tomar in the motor accident, along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11353 2 MA-1160-2019 till its realization.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Claims Tribunal has committed a grave error in awarding inadequate compensation.
It is further contended that the Tribunal erred in holding that the deceased did not die as a result of the motor accident.
It is submitted that the accident occurred on 24.05.2012, and the deceased succumbed to the injuries on 16.08.2012 due to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
Therefore, the finding of the Claims Tribunal that the death was not caused by the motor accident is erroneous.
It is further argued that it is a settled principle of law that post-mortem is not mandatory in such cases.
On these grounds, it is prayed that the findings of the Claims Tribunal be set aside and just and reasonable compensation be awarded.
6. Per contra , learned counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
He supports the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
8.

Upon due consideration of the rival submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the entire record, it is apparent that the accident in question occurred on 24.05.2012,
wherein the deceased sustained grievous injuries.
However, the deceased expired subsequently on 16.08.2012.

The appellants have failed to adduce cogent, reliable, and convincing evidence to establish a proximate nexus between the injuries sustained in the said accident and the eventual death of the deceased.

A careful perusal of paragraphs 20, 21, 22, and 23 of the impugned award reveals that the Claims Tribunal has meticulously examined and appreciated the evidence available on record in its proper NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11353 3 MA-1160-2019 perspective.
The Tribunal has, upon due analysis, rightly concluded that the death of the deceased cannot be attributed to the injuries sustained in the motor accident.
In view of the aforesaid, this Court finds no perversity, illegality, or infirmity in the findings so recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

Consequently, no interference is called for with respect to the said finding.
9.

However, with regard to the enhancement of compensation, this Court, upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, perusing the record, and considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, deems it appropriate to enhance the compensation by a lump sum amount of Rs.
1,00,000/-.
10.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed .
The appellants shall be entitled to an additional sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain unaltered.
11. The present appeal stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
